tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit

Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# OBSI repo scaffold — plan

## Context
Empty repo (no commits) holding only `obsi-methodology.md` (the spec, sha256 `07acba3c91d8e7605949a71c5657a04309324ded56ed1d9a30eac8f9504ee655`), `sample-input.json` (at repo root, not `data/`) and `.idea/`. - `package-info.java` per package with Javadoc citing spec section:

Reads `file_path` / `notebook_path` / `command`; resolves relative paths against payload `cwd`.

# Agent rules (CLAUDE.md is a symlink to this file)

## Source of truth
- `obsi-methodology.md` is the spec and the source of truth. Never edit it (`SpecIntegrityTest` pins its SHA-256).
- Never edit anything in `src/test/resources/expected/`. Hooks and permission rules block both.
- Cite the spec section or equation in code next to the logic it implements, e.g. `// §2: PED > 5% excludes`, `// Eq. 2`. Keep `docs/spec-trace.md` up to date.
- If the spec is ambiguous or silent, add an entry to `docs/decisions.md` and stop. Don't decide it yourself and don't encode a guess in code or tests.

## Workflow
- Write tests before code. A test written ahead of its implementation gets `@Tag("wip")`. Remove the tag once it passes.
- jqwik properties: use `net.jqwik.api.Tag`, because JUnit's `@Tag` has no effect on `@Property`. Tag slow properties `slow`.
- Fast tests: `./mvnw -q test -DexcludedGroups=slow`. Full suite: `./build.sh`. The Stop hook runs `verify -DexcludedGroups=wip`.

## I/O
- Results go to stdout as JSON. Errors go to stderr as JSON. Nothing else goes to stdout.
- `run.sh` must work offline. It only runs `target/obsi.jar`.

## Numbers
- Use `BigDecimal` for prices and sizes, never `double`.
- Parse JSON numbers as `BigDecimal`: enable `DeserializationFeature.USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS` and read with `JsonNode.decimalValue()`, so `100.2` never passes through a double.
- Do boundary checks without division:
  - PED limit (§2): `|m - med| * 100 <= 5 * med` passes.
  - midSV cutoff (Eq. 1f / Eq. 2): `midSV <= D` is `askPV <= (1 + D) * midPV`.
- Group prices with `compareTo`, using `TreeMap<BigDecimal, …>`. Never use `equals` or `HashMap`, because `100.0` and `100` are different under `equals`.

# Open decisions

Questions the spec (`obsi-methodology.md`) leaves open. **Nothing here is decided.** Each entry stays `Open` until a human resolves it. Agents add entries but never fill in a resolution.

Format: ID, question, spec reference, options seen so far, status.

## Input

### D-01 String numbers
Is a price or size given as a JSON string (`"100"`) "numeric" for the §2 entry screen, or is it discarded?
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "discard a price/size entry if either component is not numeric".
- Options: accept numeric strings / discard entry.
- Status: Open

### D-02 Duplicate exchange names
What happens when two books share an `exchange` name?
- Spec: silent. §2 treats each book as "a constituent exchange book".
- Options: treat as separate books / merge / input error / exclude both.
- Status: Open

### D-03 Unreadable books in `excludedExchanges`
Should a book whose structure can't be read (§2) be listed among excluded exchanges, and how is it identified if it has no readable `exchange` name? Note that `excludedExchanges` is not a spec term; the output format is D-08.
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "Exclude a book if its structure cannot be read".
- Status: Open

### D-04 Unknown input fields
Are unknown top-level, book-level or entry-level fields ignored or rejected?
- Spec: silent. §2 only says "Malformed top-level input ... are input errors".
- Status: Open

### D-05 Entry shape
The `[price, size]` array shape is only shown by the sample. How are arrays of length ≠ 2, `null`, booleans, `NaN`/`Infinity` and nested arrays handled: discarded entry (§2 entry screen) or unreadable book (§2 book screen)?
- Status: Open

### D-06 Top-level vs book-level malformation
Where is the line between "malformed top-level input" (input error) and "structure cannot be read" (book excluded)? Examples: `books` is not an array; a book is a string; a book is missing `bids`; `bids` is an object.
- Spec: §2 ¶1, §6.
- Status: Open

### D-07 Required top-level fields and `calculationTime`
Which top-level fields are required? The spec names only `calculationTime` (§1). Must `calculationTime` parse as ISO-8601, and is it echoed in the output? Is an empty `books` array an input error, or the §6 failure "no constituent book survives screening"?
- Status: Open

## Output and CLI

### D-08 Output schema, error schema, exit codes
The spec defines no output format. Field names, how excluded books and their reasons are reported, the error JSON shape, and exit codes for input errors vs calculation failures are all undefined. (The scaffold currently prints `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED",...}` and exits 1.)
- Spec: §6 "Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot."
- Status: Open

### D-09 Where `--verbose` output goes
Should diagnostic output (intermediate books, curves, v_T) go to stderr, into an extra field in the stdout JSON, or to a file? And is it JSON or text?
- Constraint: stdout must remain a single JSON result.
- Status: Open

### D-10 CLI input
Is the input a path argument, stdin, or both? What happens with missing or extra arguments?
- Status: Open

## Book handling

### D-11 Unsorted levels and duplicate prices within one book
Is "best bid" the highest bid price, or the first entry as given? Are duplicate prices within a single book summed before the §2 checks? (§3 sums only across books.)
- Spec: §1 notation, §2 ¶1, §3 ¶1.
- Status: Open

### D-12 Does "survives screening" (§6) include the PED screen?
§2 groups entry, book and PED checks under "screens", but §2's first paragraph calls only the first set "checks". This matters for which failure reason is reported when every book is a PED outlier.
- Status: Open

## Numerics

### D-13 double vs BigDecimal for the exponential weights
`λe^{-λv}` and `NF` (§5) involve `exp`, which `BigDecimal` has no built-in for. Options: compute weights in `double`; use a BigDecimal series to a fixed precision. HALF_UP at two decimals (§5) is sensitive when the unrounded value sits near `x.xx5`.
- Status: Open

### D-14 MathContext for divisions
What precision and rounding apply to the OBSI sum divided by NF, and to any other non-terminating division? (Medians and mids divide by 2 and are exact. PED and midSV checks avoid division, see AGENTS.md.)
- Status: Open

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop: run the full suite except @Tag("wip") before Claude finishes a turn. If it fails, block
# the stop so Claude fixes it. Tests tagged wip (written before their code) never block.
# Loop guard: stop_hook_active is true when Claude is already continuing because of this hook,
# so a second failure lets the turn end instead of looping (Claude Code also caps consecutive
# blocks at 8).
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(pwd)}"
payload="$(cat)"
[[ "$(jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false' <<<"$payload")" == "true" ]] && exit 0

cd "$ROOT" || exit 0
STAMP="target/.stop-hook-green"
# Skip when nothing the suite depends on has changed since the last green run.
if [[ -f "$STAMP" ]] && [[ -z "$(find src pom.xml README.md proposal.md obsi-methodology.md \
      -newer "$STAMP" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

if output="$(./mvnw -q verify -DexcludedGroups=wip 2>&1)"; then
  mkdir -p target && touch "$STAMP"
  exit 0
fi
jq -n --arg out "$(tail -n 80 <<<"$output")" \
  '{decision: "block", reason: ("Test suite failed (./mvnw -q verify -DexcludedGroups=wip). Fix it, or tag a test written ahead of its code with @Tag(\"wip\"):\n" + $out)}'
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop / SessionEnd: copy this session's transcript (and its subagent transcripts) into
docs/ai-sessions/claude-code/<session_id>/. Idempotent: each run overwrites the previous copy.
Never blocks; errors are reported on stderr only."""
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys


def main():
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
        src = payload.get("transcript_path")
        session = payload.get("session_id")
        if not src or not session or not os.path.isfile(src):
            return
        root = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or payload.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
        dest = os.path.join(root, "docs", "ai-sessions", "claude-code", session)
        os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(dest, "transcript.jsonl"))
        subagents = os.path.join(os.path.splitext(src)[0], "subagents")
        if os.path.isdir(subagents):
            out = os.path.join(dest, "subagents")
            os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
            for name in os.listdir(subagents):
                if name.endswith((".jsonl", ".meta.json")):
                    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(subagents, name), os.path.join(out, name))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"save_transcript.py: {e}", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
    sys.exit(0)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop: run the full suite except @Tag("wip") before Claude finishes a turn. If it fails, block
# the stop so Claude fixes it. Tests tagged wip (written before their code) never block.
# Loop guard: stop_hook_active is true when Claude is already continuing because of this hook,
# so a second failure lets the turn end instead of looping (Claude Code also caps consecutive
# blocks at 8).
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(pwd)}"
payload="$(cat)"
[[ "$(jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false' <<<"$payload")" == "true" ]] && exit 0

cd "$ROOT" || exit 0
STAMP="target/.stop-hook-green"
# Skip when nothing the suite depends on has changed since the last green run.
if [[ -f "$STAMP" ]] && [[ -z "$(find src pom.xml README.md proposal.md obsi-methodology.md \
      -newer "$STAMP" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

if output="$(./mvnw -q verify -DexcludedGroups=wip 2>&1)"; then
  mkdir -p target && touch "$STAMP"
  exit 0
fi
jq -n --arg out "$(tail -n 80 <<<"$output")" \
  '{decision: "block", reason: ("Test suite failed (./mvnw -q verify -DexcludedGroups=wip). Fix it, or tag a test written ahead of its code with @Tag(\"wip\"):\n" + $out)}'
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop / SessionEnd: copy this session's transcript (and its subagent transcripts) into
docs/ai-sessions/claude-code/<session_id>/. Idempotent: each run overwrites the previous copy.
Never blocks; errors are reported on stderr only."""
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys


def main():
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
        src = payload.get("transcript_path")
        session = payload.get("session_id")
        if not src or not session or not os.path.isfile(src):
            return
        root = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or payload.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
        dest = os.path.join(root, "docs", "ai-sessions", "claude-code", session)
        os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(dest, "transcript.jsonl"))
        subagents = os.path.join(os.path.splitext(src)[0], "subagents")
        if os.path.isdir(subagents):
            out = os.path.join(dest, "subagents")
            os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
            for name in os.listdir(subagents):
                if name.endswith((".jsonl", ".meta.json")):
                    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(subagents, name), os.path.join(out, name))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"save_transcript.py: {e}", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
    sys.exit(0)

# Self-test for guard_protected.py: feeds PreToolUse payloads and checks allow/deny.
# Usage: .claude/hooks/test_guard.sh
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
GUARD="$ROOT/.claude/hooks/guard_protected.py"
export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$ROOT"
fail=0

run() { # expected(allow|deny) tool field value [cwd]
  local want="$1" tool="$2" field="$3" value="$4" cwd="${5:-$ROOT}" out got
  out="$(jq -n --arg t "$tool" --arg f "$field" --arg v "$value" --arg c "$cwd" \
          '{hook_event_name:"PreToolUse", cwd:$c, tool_name:$t, tool_input:{($f):$v}}' \
        | python3 "$GUARD")"
  if grep -q '"permissionDecision": "deny"' <<<"$out"; then got=deny; else got=allow; fi
  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then
    printf 'ok    %-5s %-6s %s\n' "$want" "$tool" "$value"
  else
    printf 'FAIL  want %s got %s: %s %s\n' "$want" "$got" "$tool" "$value"; fail=1
  fi
}

E=src/test/resources/expected
# File tools
run deny  Write        file_path     "$ROOT/$E/probe.json"
run deny  Edit         file_path     "$ROOT/obsi-methodology.md"

The scaffold is done and nothing is committed. All four checks pass: the build, the offline `run.sh` exit code, the spec hash, and the protected-path blocking (with one caveat on Edit, below).

## Checks
- **Build:** `./build.sh` exits 0 and produces `target/obsi.jar` (about 2.4 MB, Jackson bundled in).
- **run.sh:** I ran it with networking switched off, on `data/sample-input.json`. It exits 1, stdout is empty, and stderr is `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED","message":"OBSI calculation is not implemented yet"}`.
- **Spec:** the hash is unchanged (`07acba3c…ee655`), and `expected/` holds only `.gitkeep`.
- **Bash blocking:** the hook blocked `echo … > src/test/resources/expected/probe.json` in this session. It also blocked an `ln -s` of mine that pointed at `expected/`.
- **Edit/Write blocking (caveat):** a Write to `expected/` was also blocked, but by the permission `deny` rule, which runs before the hook. The hook itself never saw that call. The hook's own Edit/Write checks are covered by `.claude/hooks/test_guard.sh` (36 cases, all pass) rather than a live call.
- **Test hooks:** I checked both with a throwaway failing test, now deleted. The post-edit hook fired on its own and reported the failure. The Stop hook blocked on the failure, let the turn end when `stop_hook_active` was true, and passed once the test was tagged `wip`.
- **Guard bug fixed:** testing found that the guard split `2>&1` at the `&`. It's fixed, with regression cases added.

## What I changed from your instructions
- **Moved** `sample-input.json` into `data/`, as you chose.
- **README and proposal:** you rejected my first versions, so they're now one-line placeholders.
- **Second blocking layer:** `.claude/settings.json` also has `permissions.deny` rules for the spec and `expected/**`, besides the hook.
- **Line endings:** added `.gitattributes` so line-ending conversion can't break the spec hash or the golden files.
- **"Fast tests" (my choice):** everything except `@Tag("slow")`, run only when the edit touches `src/` or `pom.xml`. `wip` tests stay in, so you see the red test while developing. Only the Stop hook excludes `wip`.
- **Stop hook skip:** it skips the run when nothing under `src/`, `pom.xml`, the README, the proposal or the spec changed since the last green run.
- **Transcript location:** sessions are saved to `docs/ai-sessions/claude-code/<session>/`, including subagent transcripts.
- **Extra rules in `AGENTS.md`:**
  - Jackson must read numbers as BigDecimal (`USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS`). Otherwise `100.2` passes through a `double` before your BigDecimal rules apply.
  - jqwik properties need `net.jqwik.api.Tag`, because JUnit's `@Tag` doesn't apply to them. This matters for the `wip` exclusion.
- **`deliverables.md`** is based on your message only. Items I couldn't source are marked "confirm against brief".

## What the spec doesn't cover (all added to `docs/decisions.md` as open questions)
- **No output format at all.** `excludedExchanges` isn't a spec term, and there's no error schema, exit codes, or CLI contract (path argument or stdin).
- **Required top-level fields aren't listed.** Also open: the `calculationTime` format, and whether an empty `books` array is an input error or the §6 "no book survives" failure.
- **Entry shape `[price, size]` comes only from the sample.** Wrong-length arrays, null, booleans and NaN aren't covered.

- **Unsorted levels or duplicate prices within one book:** is "best bid" the highest price or the first entry?
- **Whether "survives screening" in §6 includes the 5% deviation check.**
- **Precision (MathContext) for the division by NF**, alongside your double-vs-BigDecimal question for the weights.
- **Not a gap, but easy to get wrong:** Eq. 2 takes the **last** cutoff crossing (`max`), not the first. I flagged it in `docs/spec-trace.md` and in the reviewer subagent's checklist.

- **The guard's limits:**
  - It's deliberately conservative: any command that names the spec and also has a redirect is blocked, even `cat spec > /tmp/x`.
  - It doesn't catch git commands that restore files without naming paths, like `git checkout .`.
  - It's a safety net, not a security boundary.

# Brief

Notes from the take-home brief, only the parts the code has to follow. The calculation itself is in
obsi-methodology.md. Anything unclear goes to decisions.md.

## What to build

Task 1 is the methodology applied to one snapshot, with failures reported as described below, and a
README for the next Index Engineer. Task 2 is the PED extension: compare two approaches in proposal.md
and implement the chosen one behind `--new-ped`.

No live feed, publishing or deployment. Readable and testable is the bar.

## CLI

Java 25, takes one local JSON path. The repo root needs executable build.sh and run.sh, mvnw with the
wrapper files, and pom.xml. build.sh runs first and has to leave everything ready for run.sh. After
that, both of these must work offline with just Java 25:

    ./run.sh data/sample-input.json
    ./run.sh --new-ped data/new-ped.json

The reviewer may also run it against other files in data/.

## Input

    {
      "calculationTime": "2026-...Z",          ISO-8601 UTC, time of the snapshot
      "books": [
        {
          "exchange": "A",                     unique, nonempty
          "bids": [[price, size], ...],
          "asks": [[price, size], ...]
        }
      ]
    }

Price is USD per XYZ, size is XYZ, both positive JSON numbers. data/sample-input.json is the reference.

## Output

Success: one JSON object on stdout, exit 0.

    {
      "index": "OBSI",
      "calculationTime": "<same as input>",
      "status": "published",
      "value": "100.00",
      "metadata": {
        "utilizedDepth": "1",
        "excludedExchanges": []
      }
    }

value is a string with two decimals. utilizedDepth is a decimal string in XYZ. excludedExchanges lists
the screened-out exchanges in the same order they appear in the input.

Failure: one JSON object on stderr, nonzero exit.

    {
      "index": "OBSI",
      "calculationTime": "<same as input, or null>",
      "status": "failed",
      "reason": "<short explanation>"
    }

calculationTime is null when the input itself doesn't conform.

The result stays on its own stream and diagnostics go somewhere else (D6 in decisions.md).

## Task 2

What the PM raised in the meeting:

- PED exists to catch an exchange that deviates because of a temporary problem of its own.
- Weekends have less liquidity, so the static limit was set wide to cope. That probably makes it too
  wide on weekdays.
- Some of the newly added exchanges sit at a constant premium over the median. The PM thinks that's
  market structure, not bad data, and wants it left out of PED.
- Token unlocks are announced ahead of time. Liquidity goes up for roughly 48h from the start of the
  unlock, and the PM wants PED much tighter in that window.
- Not everything needs solving. Prefer something with a financial rationale that is easy to explain
  to clients.

What has to be delivered: proposal.md comparing two approaches and explaining the choice (it can cover
only some of the points). `--new-ped` runs the chosen approach; without the flag the original 5% rule
stays. If the input JSON gains or changes fields, document them in proposal.md and put a sample in
data/new-ped.json. If nothing changes, data/new-ped.json is just a copy of sample-input.json.

## Submission

Working code with deterministic tests and both fixtures. proposal.md and README.md, 1000 words max each.
The README covers implemented steps, assumptions, tests, production gaps and why each library was chosen
(keep them small and well known). The full AI sessions go in ai-transcript.md or as native exports,
redacting only secrets and personal data, and saying so when something was redacted. If something isn't
finished, ship it anyway and say what's missing.

2	
3	Questions the spec (`obsi-methodology.md`) leaves open. **Nothing here is decided.** Each entry stays `Open` until a human resolves it. Agents add entries but never fill in a resolution.

5	Format: ID, question, spec reference, options seen so far, status.
6	
7	## Input
8	
9	### D-01 String numbers
10	Is a price or size given as a JSON string (`"100"`) "numeric" for the §2 entry screen, or is it discarded?
11	- Spec: §2 ¶1 "discard a price/size entry if either component is not numeric".
12	- Options: accept numeric strings / discard entry.
13	- Status: Open
14	
15	### D-02 Duplicate exchange names
16	What happens when two books share an `exchange` name?
17	- Spec: silent. §2 treats each book as "a constituent exchange book".
18	- Options: treat as separate books / merge / input error / exclude both.
19	- Status: Open
20	
21	### D-03 Unreadable books in `excludedExchanges`
22	Should a book whose structure can't be read (§2) be listed among excluded exchanges, and how is it identified if it has no readable `exchange` name? Note that `excludedExchanges` is not a spec term; the output format is D-08.
23	- Spec: §2 ¶1 "Exclude a book if its structure cannot be read".
24	- Status: Open
25	
26	### D-04 Unknown input fields
27	Are unknown top-level, book-level or entry-level fields ignored or rejected?
28	- Spec: silent. §2 only says "Malformed top-level input ... are input errors".
29	- Status: Open
30	
31	### D-05 Entry shape
32	The `[price, size]` array shape is only shown by the sample. How are arrays of length ≠ 2, `null`, booleans, `NaN`/`Infinity` and nested arrays handled: discarded entry (§2 entry screen) or unreadable book (§2 book screen)?
33	- Status: Open
34	
35	### D-06 Top-level vs book-level malformation
36	Where is the line between "malformed top-level input" (input error) and "structure cannot be read" (book excluded)? Examples: `books` is not an array; a book is a string; a book is missing `bids`; `bids` is an object.
37	- Spec: §2 ¶1, §6.
38	- Status: Open
39	
40	### D-07 Required top-level fields and `calculationTime`
41	Which top-level fields are required? The spec names only `calculationTime` (§1). Must `calculationTime` parse as ISO-8601, and is it echoed in the output? Is an empty `books` array an input error, or the §6 failure "no constituent book survives screening"?
42	- Status: Open
43	
44	## Output and CLI
45	
46	### D-08 Output schema, error schema, exit codes
47	The spec defines no output format. Field names, how excluded books and their reasons are reported, the error JSON shape, and exit codes for input errors vs calculation failures are all undefined. (The scaffold currently prints `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED",...}` and exits 1.)
48	- Spec: §6 "Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot."
49	- Status: Open
50	
51	### D-09 Where `--verbose` output goes
52	Should diagnostic output (intermediate books, curves, v_T) go to stderr, into an extra field in the stdout JSON, or to a file? And is it JSON or text?
53	- Constraint: stdout must remain a single JSON result.
54	- Status: Open
55	
56	### D-10 CLI input
57	Is the input a path argument, stdin, or both? What happens with missing or extra arguments?
58	- Status: Open
59	
60	## Book handling
61	
62	### D-11 Unsorted levels and duplicate prices within one book
63	Is "best bid" the highest bid price, or the first entry as given? Are duplicate prices within a single book summed before the §2 checks? (§3 sums only across books.)
64	- Spec: §1 notation, §2 ¶1, §3 ¶1.
65	- Status: Open
66	
67	### D-12 Does "survives screening" (§6) include the PED screen?
68	§2 groups entry, book and PED checks under "screens", but §2's first paragraph calls only the first set "checks". This matters for which failure reason is reported when every book is a PED outlier.
69	- Status: Open
70	
71	## Numerics
72	
73	### D-13 double vs BigDecimal for the exponential weights
74	`λe^{-λv}` and `NF` (§5) involve `exp`, which `BigDecimal` has no built-in for. Options: compute weights in `double`; use a BigDecimal series to a fixed precision. HALF_UP at two decimals (§5) is sensitive when the unrounded value sits near `x.xx5`.
75	- Status: Open
76	
77	### D-14 MathContext for divisions
78	What precision and rounding apply to the OBSI sum divided by NF, and to any other non-terminating division? (Medians and mids divide by 2 and are exact. PED and midSV checks avoid division, see AGENTS.md.)
79	- Status: Open

The spec defines no output format. Field names, how excluded books and their reasons are reported, the error JSON shape, and exit codes for input errors vs calculation failures are all undefined. (The scaffold currently prints `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED",...}` and exits 1.)
- Spec: §6 "Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot."
- Status: Open

### D-09 Where `--verbose` output goes
Should diagnostic output (intermediate books, curves, v_T) go to stderr, into an extra field in the stdout JSON, or to a file? And is it JSON or text?
- Constraint: stdout must remain a single JSON result.
- Status: Open

### D-10 CLI input
Is the input a path argument, stdin, or both? What happens with missing or extra arguments?
- Status: Open

## Book handling

### D-11 Unsorted levels and duplicate prices within one book
Is "best bid" the highest bid price, or the first entry as given? Are duplicate prices within a single book summed before the §2 checks? (§3 sums only across books.)
- Spec: §1 notation, §2 ¶1, §3 ¶1.
- Status: Open

### D-12 Does "survives screening" (§6) include the PED screen?
§2 groups entry, book and PED checks under "screens", but §2's first paragraph calls only the first set "checks". This matters for which failure reason is reported when every book is a PED outlier.
- Status: Open

## Numerics

### D-13 double vs BigDecimal for the exponential weights
`λe^{-λv}` and `NF` (§5) involve `exp`, which `BigDecimal` has no built-in for. Options: compute weights in `double`; use a BigDecimal series to a fixed precision. HALF_UP at two decimals (§5) is sensitive when the unrounded value sits near `x.xx5`.
- Status: Open

### D-14 MathContext for divisions
What precision and rounding apply to the OBSI sum divided by NF, and to any other non-terminating division? (Medians and mids divide by 2 and are exact. PED and midSV checks avoid division, see AGENTS.md.)
- Status: Open

# Open decisions

Questions the spec (`obsi-methodology.md`) leaves open. **Nothing here is decided.** Each entry stays `Open` until a human resolves it. Agents add entries but never fill in a resolution.

Format: ID, question, spec reference, options seen so far, status.

## Input

### D-01 String numbers
Is a price or size given as a JSON string (`"100"`) "numeric" for the §2 entry screen, or is it discarded?
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "discard a price/size entry if either component is not numeric".
- Options: accept numeric strings / discard entry.
- Status: Open

### D-02 Duplicate exchange names
What happens when two books share an `exchange` name?
- Spec: silent. §2 treats each book as "a constituent exchange book".
- Options: treat as separate books / merge / input error / exclude both.
- Status: Open

### D-03 Unreadable books in `excludedExchanges`
Should a book whose structure can't be read (§2) be listed among excluded exchanges, and how is it identified if it has no readable `exchange` name? Note that `excludedExchanges` is not a spec term; the output format is D-08.
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "Exclude a book if its structure cannot be read".
- Status: Open

### D-04 Unknown input fields
Are unknown top-level, book-level or entry-level fields ignored or rejected?
- Spec: silent. §2 only says "Malformed top-level input ... are input errors".
- Status: Open

### D-05 Entry shape
The `[price, size]` array shape is only shown by the sample. How are arrays of length ≠ 2, `null`, booleans, `NaN`/`Infinity` and nested arrays handled: discarded entry (§2 entry screen) or unreadable book (§2 book screen)?
- Status: Open

### D-06 Top-level vs book-level malformation
Where is the line between "malformed top-level input" (input error) and "structure cannot be read" (book excluded)? Examples: `books` is not an array; a book is a string; a book is missing `bids`; `bids` is an object.
- Spec: §2 ¶1, §6.
- Status: Open

### D-07 Required top-level fields and `calculationTime`
Which top-level fields are required? The spec names only `calculationTime` (§1). Must `calculationTime` parse as ISO-8601, and is it echoed in the output? Is an empty `books` array an input error, or the §6 failure "no constituent book survives screening"?
- Status: Open

## Output and CLI

### D-08 Output schema, error schema, exit codes
The spec defines no output format. Field names, how excluded books and their reasons are reported, the error JSON shape, and exit codes for input errors vs calculation failures are all undefined. (The scaffold currently prints `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED",...}` and exits 1.)
- Spec: §6 "Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot."
- Status: Open

### D-09 Where `--verbose` output goes
Should diagnostic output (intermediate books, curves, v_T) go to stderr, into an extra field in the stdout JSON, or to a file? And is it JSON or text?
- Constraint: stdout must remain a single JSON result.
- Status: Open

### D-10 CLI input
Is the input a path argument, stdin, or both? What happens with missing or extra arguments?
- Status: Open

## Book handling

### D-11 Unsorted levels and duplicate prices within one book
Is "best bid" the highest bid price, or the first entry as given? Are duplicate prices within a single book summed before the §2 checks? (§3 sums only across books.)
- Spec: §1 notation, §2 ¶1, §3 ¶1.
- Status: Open

### D-12 Does "survives screening" (§6) include the PED screen?
§2 groups entry, book and PED checks under "screens", but §2's first paragraph calls only the first set "checks". This matters for which failure reason is reported when every book is a PED outlier.
- Status: Open

## Numerics

### D-13 double vs BigDecimal for the exponential weights
`λe^{-λv}` and `NF` (§5) involve `exp`, which `BigDecimal` has no built-in for. Options: compute weights in `double`; use a BigDecimal series to a fixed precision. HALF_UP at two decimals (§5) is sensitive when the unrounded value sits near `x.xx5`.
- Status: Open

### D-14 MathContext for divisions
What precision and rounding apply to the OBSI sum divided by NF, and to any other non-terminating division? (Medians and mids divide by 2 and are exact. PED and midSV checks avoid division, see AGENTS.md.)
- Status: Open

# Open decisions

Questions that neither the spec (`obsi-methodology.md`) nor the brief (`docs/brief.md`) answers. **Agents never decide here.** Each entry stays `Open` until a human resolves it. An entry is `Partly settled by brief` when the brief answers part of it: the quoted text is settled, and the rest stays open.

Format: ID, question, spec/brief reference, options seen so far, status.

## Input

### D-01 String numbers
Is a price or size given as a JSON string (`"100"`) "numeric" for the §2 entry screen, or is it discarded?
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "discard a price/size entry if either component is not numeric".
- Options: accept numeric strings / discard entry.
- Status: Open

### D-02 Duplicate exchange names
What happens when two books share an `exchange` name?
- Spec: silent. §2 treats each book as "a constituent exchange book".
- Options: treat as separate books / merge / input error / exclude both.
- Status: Open

### D-03 Unreadable books in `excludedExchanges`
How does a book whose structure can't be read (§2) show up in `excludedExchanges`?
- Spec: §2 ¶1 "Exclude a book if its structure cannot be read".
- Settled by brief, "Output": `excludedExchanges` sits under `metadata` in the success object, and "excludedExchanges lists the screened-out exchanges in the same order they appear in the input." §2 makes an unreadable structure one of the screens. So a book with a readable `exchange` name is listed by that name, in input order.
- Still open: how a book with no readable or nonempty `exchange` name shows up (omitted / placeholder / index-based label). Also open: whether such a book makes the input non-conforming instead (see D-06; brief, "Input": `exchange` is "unique, nonempty").
- Status: Partly settled by brief

### D-04 Unknown input fields
Are unknown top-level, book-level or entry-level fields ignored or rejected?
- Spec: silent. §2 only says "Malformed top-level input ... are input errors".
- Status: Open

### D-05 Entry shape
The `[price, size]` array shape is only shown by the sample. How are arrays of length ≠ 2, `null`, booleans, `NaN`/`Infinity` and nested arrays handled: discarded entry (§2 entry screen) or unreadable book (§2 book screen)?
- Status: Open

### D-06 Top-level vs book-level malformation
Where is the line between "malformed top-level input" (input error) and "structure cannot be read" (book excluded)? Examples: `books` is not an array; a book is a string; a book is missing `bids`; `bids` is an object.
- Spec: §2 ¶1, §6.
- Status: Open

### D-07 Required top-level fields and `calculationTime`
Which top-level fields are required, what format is `calculationTime`, and is it echoed?
- Spec: §1 names only `calculationTime` ("Effective calculation time"); §2 "missing required top-level fields are input errors".
- Settled by brief, "Input": the top level is `calculationTime` and `books`. `calculationTime` is "ISO-8601 UTC, time of the snapshot". Each book has `exchange` ("unique, nonempty"), `bids` and `asks` as `[[price, size], ...]`. "Price is USD per XYZ, size is XYZ, both positive JSON numbers."
- Settled by brief, "Output": both objects carry `"calculationTime": "<same as input>"`, and on failure "<same as input, or null>". "calculationTime is null when the input itself doesn't conform."
- Still open: is an empty `books` array non-conforming input (null `calculationTime`), or the §6 failure "no constituent book survives screening"? The brief's input example doesn't say whether `books` may be empty.
- Status: Partly settled by brief

## Output and CLI

### D-08 Output schema, error schema, exit codes
The spec defines no output format. Field names, how excluded books and their reasons are reported, the error JSON shape, and exit codes for input errors vs calculation failures are all undefined. (The scaffold currently prints `{"error":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED",...}` and exits 1.)
- Spec: §6 "Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot."
- Status: Open

### D-09 Where `--verbose` output goes
Should diagnostic output (intermediate books, curves, v_T) go to stderr, into an extra field in the stdout JSON, or to a file? And is it JSON or text?
- Constraint: stdout must remain a single JSON result.
- Status: Open

### D-10 CLI input
Is the input a path argument, stdin, or both? What happens with missing or extra arguments?
- Status: Open

## Book handling

### D-11 Unsorted levels and duplicate prices within one book
Is "best bid" the highest bid price, or the first entry as given? Are duplicate prices within a single book summed before the §2 checks? (§3 sums only across books.)
- Spec: §1 notation, §2 ¶1, §3 ¶1.
- Status: Open

### D-12 Does "survives screening" (§6) include the PED screen?
§2 groups entry, book and PED checks under "screens", but §2's first paragraph calls only the first set "checks". This matters for which failure reason is reported when every book is a PED outlier.
- Status: Open

## Numerics

### D-13 double vs BigDecimal for the exponential weights
`λe^{-λv}` and `NF` (§5) involve `exp`, which `BigDecimal` has no built-in for. Options: compute weights in `double`; use a BigDecimal series to a fixed precision. HALF_UP at two decimals (§5) is sensitive when the unrounded value sits near `x.xx5`.
- Status: Open

### D-14 MathContext for divisions
What precision and rounding apply to the OBSI sum divided by NF, and to any other non-terminating division? (Medians and mids divide by 2 and are exact. PED and midSV checks avoid division, see AGENTS.md.)
- Status: Open

# Deliverables checklist

From `docs/brief.md`. "If something isn't finished, ship it anyway and say what's missing."

## Task 1: methodology on one snapshot
- [ ] The methodology (`obsi-methodology.md`) applied to one snapshot, with failures reported in the brief's failure shape
- [ ] Success: one JSON object on stdout, exit 0. Fields: `index`, `calculationTime`, `status: "published"`, `value` (two-decimal string), `metadata.utilizedDepth` (decimal string), `metadata.excludedExchanges` (input order)
- [ ] Failure: one JSON object on stderr, nonzero exit. Fields: `index`, `calculationTime` (null when the input doesn't conform), `status: "failed"`, `reason`
- [ ] Diagnostics never share a stream with the result (D-09)

## Task 2: PED extension
- [ ] `proposal.md` compares two approaches and explains the choice. It may cover only some of the PM's points; prefer a financial rationale that's easy to explain to clients
- [ ] `--new-ped` runs the chosen approach. Without the flag, the original 5% rule is unchanged
- [ ] Any new or changed input fields are documented in `proposal.md`
- [ ] `data/new-ped.json`: a sample input for `--new-ped`. If the input format doesn't change, it's a copy of `data/sample-input.json`

## Repo and CLI
- [ ] Executable `build.sh` and `run.sh`, `mvnw` with the wrapper files, and `pom.xml` at the repo root
- [ ] `build.sh` runs first and leaves everything ready for `run.sh`
- [ ] After the build, these work offline with only Java 25:
  - `./run.sh data/sample-input.json`
  - `./run.sh --new-ped data/new-ped.json`
- [ ] Works on other inputs a reviewer drops into `data/`
- [ ] Deterministic tests, and both fixtures (`data/sample-input.json`, `data/new-ped.json`)
- [ ] `obsi-methodology.md` unchanged (`SpecIntegrityTest`), `src/test/resources/expected/` unchanged
- [ ] No `@Tag("wip")` tests left (they would fail `build.sh`)

## README.md (for the next Index Engineer)
- [ ] ≤ 1000 words (`DeliverableWordLimitTest`)
- [ ] Implemented steps
- [ ] Assumptions, including how each `docs/decisions.md` entry was resolved
- [ ] Tests: what is covered and how to run them
- [ ] Production gaps (no live feed, publishing or deployment are in scope) and anything unfinished
- [ ] Libraries, and why each was chosen. Keep them small and well known: Jackson, JUnit 5, AssertJ, jqwik

## proposal.md
- [ ] ≤ 1000 words (`DeliverableWordLimitTest`)
- [ ] Contents as in Task 2 above

## AI sessions
- [ ] Full sessions in `ai-transcript.md` or as native exports in `docs/ai-sessions/`
  - Claude Code sessions are saved there automatically by the Stop/SessionEnd hook
  - claude.ai sessions must be **exported manually** into `docs/ai-sessions/`
- [ ] `ai-transcript.md`: key moments table filled in
- [ ] Redaction: remove only secrets and personal data (e.g. email addresses, tokens, personal paths), and **say so wherever something was redacted**. Check every saved transcript before committing

| ID | Section | Clause | Code | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P.1 | Preamble | OBSI measures the USD price of XYZ at effective time T, using the books in one captured snapshot | TBD | TBD |
| P.2 | Preamble | Each snapshot is evaluated independently | TBD | TBD |
| P.3 | Preamble | Baseline orderbook deviation limit is 5% | TBD | TBD |
| 1.1 | §1 | T is `calculationTime` in the input (D-07) | TBD | TBD |
| 1.2 | §1 | Spacing s = 1 XYZ | TBD | TBD |
| 1.3 | §1 | Mid-spread cutoff D = 0.005 (0.5%) | TBD | TBD |
| 1.4 | §1 | v is cumulative XYZ volume, in multiples of s | TBD | TBD |
| 1.5 | §1 | Exchange e is one book in the snapshot (D-02) | TBD | TBD |
| 1.6 | §1 | m_{T,e} is the top-of-book mid, determined before consolidation | TBD | TBD |
| 1.7 | §1 | Median is of structurally valid book mids; mean of middle two when count is even | TBD | TBD |
| 1.8 | §1 | PED is compared with the 5% limit | TBD | TBD |
| 1.9 | §1 | A_T: consolidated asks, ascending price, raw uncapped sizes | TBD | TBD |
| 1.10 | §1 | B_T: consolidated bids, descending price, raw uncapped sizes | TBD | TBD |
| 1.11 | §1 | v_T is determined by Eq. 2 | TBD | TBD |
| 1.12 | §1 | λ = 1/(0.3·v_T) | TBD | TBD |
| 1.13 | §1 | NF is the sum of weights through v_T | TBD | TBD |
| 1.14 | §1 | Prices are USD per XYZ; sizes and depths are in XYZ | TBD | TBD |
| 1.15 | §1 | A_T and B_T are the levels remaining after screens, consolidation and uncrossing | TBD | TBD |
| 1.16 | §1 | No order size cap applies | TBD | TBD |
| 2.1 | §2 | Discard a price/size entry if either component is not numeric (D-01, D-05) | TBD | TBD |
| 2.2 | §2 | Discard a price/size entry if either component is not strictly positive | TBD | TBD |
| 2.3 | §2 | Exclude a book if its structure cannot be read (D-03, D-06) | TBD | TBD |
| 2.4 | §2 | Exclude a book if either side is empty after entry screening | TBD | TBD |
| 2.5 | §2 | Exclude a book if its best bid ≥ its best ask (D-11) | TBD | TBD |
| 2.6 | §2 | Apply these checks to each book before combining exchanges | TBD | TBD |
| 2.7 | §2 | Malformed top-level input is an input error (D-06) | TBD | TBD |
| 2.8 | §2 | Missing required top-level fields are an input error (D-07) | TBD | TBD |
| 2.9 | §2 | For each structurally valid book, m = (b_best + a_best) / 2 | TBD | TBD |
| 2.10 | §2 | Median of those mids; average middle two for an even number of books | TBD | TBD |
| 2.11 | §2 | PED = 100·\|m − median\| / median % | TBD | TBD |
| 2.12 | §2 | Exclude a book only if PED > 5% | TBD | TBD |
| 2.13 | §2 | A book at exactly 5% passes | TBD | TBD |
| 2.14 | §2 | Deviation check per snapshot, using only that snapshot's books | TBD | TBD |
| 2.15 | §2 | No reentry state and no half-limit test | TBD | TBD |
| 3.1 | §3 | Combine the surviving books into one book | TBD | TBD |
| 3.2 | §3 | Sum sizes at identical bid prices and, separately, at identical ask prices | TBD | TBD |
| 3.3 | §3 | Order bids highest to lowest and asks lowest to highest | TBD | TBD |
| 3.4 | §3 | While best bid ≥ best ask, subtract the smaller of their sizes from both levels | TBD | TBD |
| 3.5 | §3 | Remove every level whose residual size becomes zero | TBD | TBD |
| 3.6 | §3 | Repeat until best bid < best ask | TBD | TBD |
| 3.7 | §3 | Calculation fails if either side is exhausted | TBD | TBD |
| 4.1 | §4 Eq. 1a | Unspaced askPV(v) = ap_{j+1} where Σ_{i≤j} as_i < v and Σ_{i≤j+1} as_i ≥ v | TBD | TBD |
| 4.2 | §4 Eq. 1b | Unspaced bidPV(v) = bp_{j+1} where Σ_{i≤j} bs_i < v and Σ_{i≤j+1} bs_i ≥ v | TBD | TBD |
| 4.3 | §4 | j ≥ 0; an empty sum equals zero | TBD | TBD |
| 4.4 | §4 Eq. 1c | askPV(v) = unspaced askPV(s·⌈v/s⌉) | TBD | TBD |
| 4.5 | §4 Eq. 1d | bidPV(v) = unspaced bidPV(s·⌈v/s⌉) | TBD | TBD |
| 4.6 | §4 Eq. 1e | midPV(v) = (askPV(v) + bidPV(v)) / 2 | TBD | TBD |
| 4.7 | §4 Eq. 1f | midSV(v) = askPV(v) / midPV(v) − 1 | TBD | TBD |
| 5.1 | §5 Eq. 2 | v_T = **max** {v_i : midSV(v_i) ≤ D ∧ midSV(v_{i+1}) > D}: the last crossing, not the first | TBD | TBD |
| 5.2 | §5 Eq. 2 | v_i = i·s, i = 1, 2, … | TBD | TBD |
| 5.3 | §5 | Evaluate a candidate only when both curves are defined at v_i and v_{i+1} | TBD | TBD |
| 5.4 | §5 | λ = 1/(0.3·v_T) | TBD | TBD |

| 5.6 | §5 Eq. 3 | OBSI = Σ_{v ∈ {s, …, v_T}} midPV(v)·λe^{−λv} / NF | TBD | TBD |
| 5.7 | §5 | Round the published value to 2 dp with Java HALF_UP | TBD | TBD |
| 6.1 | §6 | Fails for malformed required input | TBD | TBD |
| 6.2 | §6 | Fails if no constituent book survives screening (D-12) | TBD | TBD |
| 6.3 | §6 | Fails if uncrossing exhausts either side | TBD | TBD |
| 6.4 | §6 | Fails if the Eq. 2 set is empty: insufficient depth to evaluate consecutive samples | TBD | TBD |
| 6.5 | §6 | Fails if the Eq. 2 set is empty: no cutoff crossing before either curve ends | TBD | TBD |
| 6.6 | §6 | Do not publish an index value for a failed snapshot (D-08) | TBD | TBD |
| 6.7 | §6 | One offline calculation from one supplied snapshot; no collection or publication infrastructure | TBD | TBD |
| 7.1 | §7 | Deviation limit 5% (consistent with P.3, 2.12) | TBD | TBD |

| 7.3 | §7 | s = 1 XYZ (consistent with 1.2) | TBD | TBD |
| 7.4 | §7 | λ = 1/(0.3·v_T) (consistent with 1.12, 5.4) | TBD | TBD |
| 7.5 | §7 | Two decimal places, Java HALF_UP (consistent with 5.7) | TBD | TBD |

The scaffold now follows the brief's failure shape, and I found three places where the brief and the spec disagree (listed below). The build passes and nothing is committed.

## Build and run
```
$ ./build.sh
build exit=0

$ ./run.sh data/sample-input.json
{"index":"OBSI","calculationTime":null,"status":"failed","reason":"calculation not implemented yet"}
run exit=1
```
The JSON goes to stderr and nothing goes to stdout.

## What changed
1. **`Main` and `run.sh`** now report failures in the brief's shape. The `run.sh` message for a missing jar uses the same shape, and I removed the "CLI contract is open" lines.
   - `MainSmokeTest` checks the field names and order, `calculationTime` null, status `failed`, a reason, and a nonzero exit. It doesn't require exit code 1, since the exact values are still open.
   - I also updated the `cli` package-info, which said the same thing.
2. **`decisions.md`:** D-03, D-07, D-08 and D-10 now quote what the brief settles and are marked "Partly settled by brief".
   - **Still open:** the exit code values (`Main` uses 1, `run.sh` uses 2 for a missing jar), the bad-argument cases, and unnamed unreadable books.
   - **Two more things left open that weren't on your list:** whether an empty `books` array is bad input or a §6 failure, and an unreadable input path. The brief covers neither.
   - **D-09:** I added the brief's diagnostics sentence. The failure result is on stderr, so that's a result stream too, and diagnostics can't safely go there either.
3. **`deliverables.md`:** rebuilt from the brief, without the "confirm" marks. It covers Task 1, Task 2 with `proposal.md` and `data/new-ped.json`, the repo and CLI, the README items, and the redaction rule.
4. **`spec-trace.md`:** new "Brief contract" table with CLI (C), input (I), output (O) and `--new-ped` (N) rows. O.6 and O.7 point at the scaffold `Main` and `MainSmokeTest`.
5. **`.gitignore`:** there's no PDF in the repo, so I added `*.pdf` rather than guess the filename. Tell me the name if you want it narrower.

## Where the brief contradicts the spec or the scaffold
- **Entry screening:** the brief says price and size are "both positive JSON numbers", and that `calculationTime` is null when the input "doesn't conform". The spec (§2) says to *discard* a non-numeric or non-positive entry and carry on. If a bad entry counts as non-conforming input, the whole snapshot fails instead. This affects D-01 and D-05.
- **Exchange names:** the brief says `exchange` is "unique, nonempty". The spec says nothing about names and excludes bad books one by one. A duplicate or empty name could mean the whole input fails, or just that book is excluded (D-02, D-03).
- **Decision numbering:** the brief points to "D6 in decisions.md" for diagnostics. In my file that's D-09, and D-06 is a different question. I noted it in D-09 but didn't renumber; that's your call.
- **"Deterministic tests" vs jqwik:** jqwik uses a random seed on every run, and its `.jqwik-database` file replays earlier failures. To meet the brief, property tests will need fixed seeds. I haven't changed this.
- **`build.sh` runs every test:** a leftover `@Tag("wip")` test would fail `build.sh`, and the brief needs the build to leave everything ready for `run.sh`. It's on the deliverables checklist.
- **`utilizedDepth` format:** the brief only gives `"1"` as an example of a "decimal string". It doesn't say how many decimal places to print. Minor, so I didn't log it as a decision.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** your edit left an empty `- ` bullet on line 9. I didn't touch it.

# Deliverables checklist

From `docs/brief.md`. "If something isn't finished, ship it anyway and say what's missing."

## Task 1: methodology on one snapshot
- [ ] The methodology (`obsi-methodology.md`) applied to one snapshot, with failures reported in the brief's failure shape
- [ ] Success: one JSON object on stdout, exit 0. Fields: `index`, `calculationTime`, `status: "published"`, `value` (two-decimal string), `metadata.utilizedDepth` (decimal string), `metadata.excludedExchanges` (input order)
- [ ] Failure: one JSON object on stderr, nonzero exit. Fields: `index`, `calculationTime` (null when the input doesn't conform), `status: "failed"`, `reason`
- [ ] Diagnostics never share a stream with the result (D-09)

## Task 2: PED extension
- [ ] `proposal.md` compares two approaches and explains the choice. It may cover only some of the PM's points; prefer a financial rationale that's easy to explain to clients
- [ ] `--new-ped` runs the chosen approach. Without the flag, the original 5% rule is unchanged
- [ ] Any new or changed input fields are documented in `proposal.md`
- [ ] `data/new-ped.json`: a sample input for `--new-ped`. If the input format doesn't change, it's a copy of `data/sample-input.json`

## Repo and CLI
- [ ] Executable `build.sh` and `run.sh`, `mvnw` with the wrapper files, and `pom.xml` at the repo root
- [ ] `build.sh` runs first and leaves everything ready for `run.sh`
- [ ] After the build, these work offline with only Java 25:
  - `./run.sh data/sample-input.json`
  - `./run.sh --new-ped data/new-ped.json`
- [ ] Works on other inputs a reviewer drops into `data/`
- [ ] Deterministic tests, and both fixtures (`data/sample-input.json`, `data/new-ped.json`)
- [ ] `obsi-methodology.md` unchanged (`SpecIntegrityTest`), `src/test/resources/expected/` unchanged
- [ ] No `@Tag("wip")` tests left (they would fail `build.sh`)

## README.md (for the next Index Engineer)
- [ ] ≤ 1000 words (`DeliverableWordLimitTest`)
- [ ] Implemented steps
- [ ] Assumptions, including how each `docs/decisions.md` entry was resolved
- [ ] Tests: what is covered and how to run them
- [ ] Production gaps (no live feed, publishing or deployment are in scope) and anything unfinished
- [ ] Libraries, and why each was chosen. Keep them small and well known: Jackson, JUnit 5, AssertJ, jqwik

## proposal.md
- [ ] ≤ 1000 words (`DeliverableWordLimitTest`)
- [ ] Contents as in Task 2 above

## AI sessions
- [ ] Full sessions in `ai-transcript.md` or as native exports in `docs/ai-sessions/`
  - Claude Code sessions are saved there automatically by the Stop/SessionEnd hook
  - claude.ai sessions must be **exported manually** into `docs/ai-sessions/`
- [ ] `ai-transcript.md`: key moments table filled in
- [ ] Redaction: remove only secrets and personal data (e.g. email addresses, tokens, personal paths), and **say so wherever something was redacted**. Check every saved transcript before committing
